content: Acneiform eruption refers to a group of skin conditions that include acne vulgaris, rosacea, folliculitis, and perioral dermatitis. These conditions are characterized by follicular eruptions that present as papules and pustules, resembling acne. The term acneiform literally means resembling acne in appearance. The terminology in this field can be complex and, at times, contradictory. Some sources consider acne vulgaris as part of the differential diagnosis for an acneiform eruption, while others classify acne vulgaris under the broader category of acneiform eruptions. The Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) system explicitly excludes perioral dermatitis from the category of acneiform eruptions. However, it does group acneiform eruptions and perioral dermatitis together under the broader classification of facial dermatoses.
